summary: Receives custom-device or TouchDesigner Pipe Out channel data over a TCP/IP stream, with optional script-command handling.
key_concepts: Pipe In CHOP receives channel data or commands over a TCP/IP pipe as either a client or a server.
Active controls connection/update behavior; data sent by a server while Active is off is lost, while pipe data may be stored until Active returns.
Queued mode uses minimum target, maximum target, maximum queue, and adjust time settings to smooth incoming samples at the cost of latency.
Incoming script commands are ignored unless Allow Incoming Scripts is enabled, which is a security-sensitive choice.
Official docs recommend Touch In CHOP for optimized TouchDesigner-to-TouchDesigner time-sliced channel transfer.
For script commands or arbitrary data packets, TCP/IP DAT or UDP In DAT is usually the preferred official path.

common_gotchas: Pipe In is a TCP/IP command stream, not the optimized time-sliced channel stream of Touch In CHOP.
A connection must be established before data is sent; the server should already be listening on the configured port.
Incoming data can include TouchDesigner scripting commands; leave script handling disabled unless that is explicitly required and trusted.
For script commands or arbitrary data packets, official docs prefer TCP/IP DAT or UDP In DAT.
For TouchDesigner-to-TouchDesigner channel transfer, Touch In CHOP is usually more optimized.
On Windows, firewall settings are a common cause of connection failures.
